text: The SEC's 1985 safe harbor in Rule 203(b)(3) allowed a limited partnership itself, rather than each of its limited partners, to be counted as a single client of the general partner acting as adviser, which is what kept hedge fund advisers below the registration threshold.
citation: Kaal and Oesterle, The History of Hedge Fund Regulation in the United States (2016). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2714974

isBasedOn.name: The History of Hedge Fund Regulation in the United States

abstract: the safe harbor provision allowed a limited partnership, rather than each of its limited partners, to be counted as a "client" of a general partner acting as investment adviser to the partnership

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: applies to exemption from registration under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940
